claims.text: The initial Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy forms a multiphase microstructure through conventional solidification.
Free-energy sampling methods such as metadynamics or umbrella sampling can be integrated with CALPHAD data to model nucleation and growth kinetics in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Parameters derived from the integrated computational framework can be used to design precise heat-treatment protocols.
Controlled cooling and annealing can be aligned with simulation-derived nucleation-barrier predictions.
The proposed processing approach can control or preset nucleation sites and phase boundaries.
The proposed intervention can alter the effective free-energy landscape experienced during phase transformation.
The intervention can lower nucleation barriers for desired phases.
The intervention can increase nucleation barriers for undesired phases.
Changing phase-specific nucleation barriers enables more predictable nucleation and growth kinetics.
Simulation-guided heat treatment will direct phase evolution toward a desired phase distribution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
The treated alloys should have a more controlled and homogeneous distribution of favored constituent phases than conventionally processed alloys.
The more controlled phase distribution should improve performance predictability.
Traditional casting and uncontrolled heat treatments alter phase proportions primarily through bulk thermal adjustments.
Unmodeled kinetic factors or multicomponent interactions could limit the method when they dominate phase transformations.
Quantitative nucleation barriers predicted in these complex alloys may not translate directly into experimental processing conditions.
